name: Low Earth Orbit (500 km, 51.6°)
explain: Standard mid-inclination low Earth orbit with low radiation and rapid round-trip passes, ideal for international space station co-planar research.
basis: Standard ISS Inclination LEO, approximate, game-balanced
description: Short ~94.6 minute period, frequent passes over mid-latitude ground stations, moderate aerodynamic drag requiring annual reboost.
commsNotes: Short 8-10 minute line-of-sight passes per station pass.
radiationNotes: Shielded by geomagnetic field (0.5 krad/year behind 3mm Al).

name: Sun-Synchronous Polar Orbit (700 km, 98.2°)
explain: Retrograde polar orbit where Earth's equatorial bulge (J2) precesses the orbital plane at ~0.9856°/day, matching Earth's revolution around the Sun.
basis: Landsat 8/9 & Sentinel-2 Reference Orbit, approximate, game-balanced
description: Consistent 10:00 AM descending solar lighting across all seasons, 16-day repeat coverage cycle for Earth land monitoring.
commsNotes: High-latitude polar stations (Svalbard, Alaska) provide 10-12 contacts per day.
radiationNotes: Auroral oval and South Atlantic Anomaly exposure (1.5 krad/year).

name: Medium Earth Orbit (20,200 km, 55°)
explain: Semi-synchronous 12-hour orbit situated between the inner and outer Van Allen radiation belts, standard for navigation satellite constellations.
basis: GPS / Galileo Constellation Orbit, approximate, game-balanced
description: 12-hour orbital period, wide planetary footprint, severe trapped electron radiation environment.
commsNotes: Continuous contact windows lasting 3 to 5 hours per station.
radiationNotes: Intense electron flux from outer Van Allen belt (15 krad/year).

name: Geostationary Equatorial Orbit (35,786 km, 0°)
explain: Circular equatorial orbit matching Earth's sidereal rotation period (23.934 hours), causing the spacecraft to remain motionless above a fixed terrestrial meridian.
basis: GOES Weather Satellite / ITU Geostationary Ring, approximate, game-balanced
description: Continuous 24-hour line-of-sight to an entire hemisphere; high delta-V required for circularization and north-south station-keeping.
commsNotes: Uninterrupted 24/7 dedicated contact link to a single fixed ground antenna.
radiationNotes: Trapped radiation belt fringes and unshielded solar cosmic rays (5.0 krad/year).

name: Molniya Highly Elliptical Orbit (500 x 39,700 km, 63.4°)
explain: Frozen-argument-of-perigee orbit where J2 apsidal drift is cancelled at critical 63.4° inclination, giving 8-hour dwell time over high northern latitudes.
basis: Molniya Orbit Mechanics / Soviet Communications Satellites, approximate, game-balanced
description: 12-hour period with slow apogee crawl over Arctic zones and rapid low-altitude perigee transit.
commsNotes: Extended 8-hour line-of-sight per orbit from northern ground stations.
radiationNotes: Passes through both inner and outer Van Allen belts every 12 hours (20 krad/year).

name: Lunar-Resonant HEO (108,000 x 375,000 km, 37°)
explain: P~13.7 day orbit locked in a 2:1 orbital resonance with the Moon's gravity, providing long-term dynamical stability, minimal station-keeping, and zero Earth occultation.
basis: NASA TESS Mission Orbit / Orbital Sciences P/2 Resonance, approximate, game-balanced
description: Continuous undisturbed photometric observing (>95% efficiency) outside Earth's shadow and thermal interference.
commsNotes: Downlinks buffered science data during rapid 16-hour perigee flybys every 13.7 days.
radiationNotes: Spends >90% of time in benign interplanetary cislunar space outside radiation belts (3.0 krad/year).

name: Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 1 Halo Orbit
explain: Quasi-periodic Lissajous halo orbit around the gravitational balance point 1.5 million km sunward from Earth, providing continuous unobstructed solar observation.
basis: NASA/ESA SOHO & DSCOVR Mission Trajectory, approximate, game-balanced
description: Permanently illuminated zero-eclipse environment sunward of Earth's magnetosphere.
commsNotes: Requires NASA Deep Space Network (DSN) 34m/70m parabolic dish scheduled tracks.
radiationNotes: Unshielded solar energetic particles and galactic cosmic rays (3.0 krad/year).

name: Low Lunar Orbit (100 km, 90°)
explain: Circular polar orbit around the Moon enabling high-resolution surface mapping and reconnaissance of permanently shadowed polar craters.
basis: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), approximate, game-balanced
description: Approximately 118-minute period subject to lunar gravitational mass concentrations (mascons) requiring active station-keeping.
commsNotes: Earth occultation during every lunar farside pass (approx 45 minutes of blackout per orbit).
radiationNotes: Direct solar cosmic ray exposure and lunar surface albedo neutrons (2.0 krad/year).

name: Low Mars Orbit (400 km, 93°)
explain: Sun-synchronous circular Martian orbit tailored for surface spectroscopy, high-resolution imaging, and landing site characterization.
basis: NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO), approximate, game-balanced
description: Solar flux drops to 586 W/m² (requires ~2.3x solar array area compared to Earth). Signal latency ranges from 4 to 22 minutes.
commsNotes: Requires Deep Space Network 70m apertures; light-time delay prevents real-time teleoperation.
radiationNotes: Unshielded Martian interplanetary cosmic ray flux (1.5 krad/year).

name: Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2 Halo Orbit
explain: Lissajous halo orbit around L2 point 1.5 million km behind Earth, providing an ultra-cold, uninterrupted dark cosmic viewing background.
basis: NASA JWST & Nancy Grace Roman Reference Orbit
description: Zero Earth occultation, deep cryogenic cold background (<50K behind 5-layer Kapton sunshield) ideal for space telescopes.
commsNotes: Continuous line-of-sight to NASA Deep Space Network 34m/70m antennas with ~5 second light delay.
radiationNotes: Unshielded interplanetary cosmic rays (3.0 krad/year); zero trapped belt radiation.

name: Lunar South Pole Powered Descent
explain: Direct powered descent and precision terminal guidance trajectory to the lunar South Pole regolith surface.
basis: ISRO Chandrayaan-3 & NASA Artemis CLPS Lander Profiles
description: Terminal braking burn reducing 1,680 m/s orbital velocity to zero with closed-loop optical hazard avoidance.
commsNotes: High-gain steerable dish direct-to-Earth or lunar orbiter relay link; periodic grazing terrain occultation.
radiationNotes: Unshielded galactic cosmic rays + secondary surface neutrons (2.0 krad/year).

name: Jovian Europa Flyby Trajectory
explain: High-velocity Jupiter-resonant orbital tour making repetitive low-altitude flybys of moon Europa while minimizing exposure to Jupiter's inner radiation belts.
basis: NASA Europa Clipper Mission Trajectory Design
description: 5.2 AU distance reduces solar irradiance to 50 W/m². High-eccentricity Jovian orbit bounds radiation dose.
commsNotes: NASA DSN 70-meter aperture essential; 43-minute one-way light delay.
radiationNotes: Severe trapped relativistic electron belts (>300 krad/year shielded inside heavy vault).

name: Mars Jezero Crater Powered Descent
explain: Atmospheric entry deceleration followed by supersonic parachute deploy and pulsed retro-rocket landing inside Jezero Crater.
basis: NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance Sky Crane Entry, Descent, and Landing Architecture
description: Terminal braking in thin CO2 atmosphere with range trigger timing and Terrain-Relative Navigation.
commsNotes: UHF relay to Mars orbiters (MRO/MAVEN) or direct X-band high-gain link with 12.5-min delay.
radiationNotes: Surface solar wind and galactic cosmic ray background (1.8 krad/year).

name: Venus Super-Critical CO2 Aerobraking Orbit
explain: High-inclination polar orbit skimming upper cloud tops for atmospheric probe release and SAR radar surface penetration.
basis: NASA Magellan & DAVINCI+ Atmospheric Descent Architecture
description: High solar irradiance (2,600 W/m²) and intense corrosive upper atmospheric friction.
commsNotes: High-power X/Ka band transmitter required to punch through dense carbon dioxide atmosphere.
radiationNotes: Solar energetic proton flares at 0.72 AU (4.0 krad/year).

name: Saturnian Titan Atmospheric Insertion
explain: Equatorial capture into Titan's dense, super-cold nitrogen atmosphere for in-situ hydrocarbon seas and dunes exploration.
basis: NASA Dragonfly Rotorcraft & Cassini-Huygens Mission Architecture
description: Extremely low solar flux (15 W/m²) and cryogenic surface (-179°C). Requires MMRTG nuclear power.
commsNotes: 70-meter DSN dishes mandatory; 70-84 minute one-way light delay dictates autonomous flight software.
radiationNotes: Magnetospherically shielded by Saturn; atmospheric shielding yields benign 0.8 krad/year.

name: Asteroid Bennu Proximity Rendezvous
explain: Microgravity proximity operations and Touch-And-Go (TAG) sample acquisition orbit around primitive carbonaceous near-Earth asteroid.
basis: NASA OSIRIS-REx & JAXA Hayabusa2 Flight Profiles
description: Ultra-low gravity (micro-g) orbital maneuvering requiring precision lidar navigation and autonomous touch-and-go sampling.
commsNotes: Continuous deep space tracking with 7-15 minute signal delay.
radiationNotes: Unshielded interplanetary solar wind and galactic cosmic rays (2.5 krad/year).
